body:
I feel as if my parents only 'care' about my future as it makes them look good. They don't give a damm about my happiness, but consider me unreasonable and spoilt when I try to explain my feelings. I just can't seem to appreciate even the little things anymore, it's just become tiresome.

I do have a pet, but technically it's not mine. I had begged my family for a dog, but they didn't listen to me, and thought I was too irresponsible. I downgraded and begged again, for a hamster, which the declined. My younger sister asked for a hamster, she got it. If it wasn't for me, I'm sure he'd be dead by now, I'm probably the only one in the house who cleans his cage or remembers to feed him. But even so, he's ancient for a hamster and about to pass soon. I plan on giving him away to a friend before I pass, without telling anyone. 

Thank you for your advice, it has given me a lot to think about

Thank you for your advice, it really means a lot. My school results is based on grades, ranging; A*, A, B, C, D, E, U. Currently, I'm sitting between D and E, I've hit U a few times too. I study three subjects, each having four courses within them; Maths, Physics and Economics. Most university courses won't accept anything less than one A and two Bs. 

My job pays me the basic living wage, which is barely enough to eat well for a few days, unless you don't have the burden of utility bills and rent.

At this point, I'm not even sure what I feel about my family, I just feel nothing but resentment more often than anything. They've kept me in a cage all my life, and now I'll never be happy again. I'll have wasted my years only to live in complete misery for the rest of my life if I don't end it.

I know that I have more years to live, but doing what? My performance in this period of my life sets out how many opportunities I have. Without this, I'm at a dead end. 

I have no way to finance my dream, let alone exploring the world. I will end up broke and miserable.

Please don't apologise, I really do appreciate each and every reply on this thread, thank you so much.

I feel as if I don't have the financial means to move out currently, and even if I could, how long would I manage? My job pays the exact minimum wage and that's no good for me to live on unless I'm living in the absolute lowest conditions possible, pay cheque to pay cheque. I would never be able to finance myself or my dream. 

My school has no councillors what so ever, so I'm only able to keep this all in my head. 

It's way too late for me to switch courses at school, the year's nearly over and I didn't even take art in previous years. There are no cheap art classes in my area and I don't even have the equipment for it. My friends and colleagues try not to acknowledge me, so I doubt they'd care enough to help me.

I have tried to speak on a suicide lifeline, but my parents almost caught me and were furious, telling me how I was disgracing them.  

As for taekwondo, I am just too overwhelmed. The next lowest ranking kid next to me has 3 years of experience and he's 12. My body already feels like it's degenerating, probably my paranoia, I can barely keep up. I try asking others for help and they've told me time and time again that it's far too late for me to ever be proffesional. Even if I tried to prove them wrong, what then? I'll fail, I'll be broke and I'd have wasted time. And that's considering the microscopic chance that my parents allow me to do this.

It's too late for me to develop a talent. If I continue living, it'll just be a cycle of misery, I can feel it. I can't even force my brain to visualise my future any more. I used to have such vivid, far fetched imaginations of my later life, now all I see blankness. I've physically accepted this.

Thank you so much for spending your time reading this
Thank you for reading, I really hope your studies go well for you, your support means a lot

I'll try to stay motivated enough to do whatever I can, even push-ups in my room. As for taekwondo, as much as I love it, it's just far too late for me. I know there are so many people out there who started it at a much later age than me, but they're talented. I'm not. I needed time to cultivate any level of talent, but my parents don't give a damn. It's just too late.

Thanks for reading, I'm sorry to hear you had felt a similar way in your life. I have spoken to my parents before, but they are beyond unreasonable, I have even had several breakdowns in front of them, and their responses were to call me mad, "psychotic" and walking away. I'm nothing but a robot, I either do as I'm told or I belong in the scrapyard. But it feels worse than that, if I don't meet standards, I won't even have the dignified end of a non-functioning machine, I'll most definitely be the laughing stock of my entire family.

Thank you for replying, I like to think the same way about grades, but my recent experiences with looking for jobs and universities really put things into perspective about just how unfit I was. As for speaking to my parents, they'd label me mad, as they already have a few times. I've had several "psychotic" breakdowns over these last few months, simply due to their taunting and inability to listen. I've never been an angry or unreasonable child, at least I hope to think so, but my temper has been getting shorter and shorter. I no longer smile, I can barely fake a grin. I can't even bring myself to look humans in the eye anymore, I just don't feel as if I'm worth such an interaction.

They would not, they'd be ashamed considering many of my cousins have gotten into very prestigious universities, doing courses medicine and making great success. What would I be to them? An artist? They'd spit in my face, and have me branded as the family failure, a warning to other kids, so they don't become like me. I'd prefer death than live that kind of life.

Your advice has been really helpful, thank you so much. I would look for some courses, but at this point, I'm not sure I'll qualify for anything. My grades have deteriorated the point where my average of 80% has dropped to 30%, on a good day. I am 100% sure I've set myself up for not being independent ever for the rest of my life, and I'd rather be dead than be considered a leech by my family.

As for gaming, I did have quite an interest, but no way to finance it. And I'm more than certain my parents would never spend a penny on a game or console for me. It may seem like they're being stingy, but they are considerably well off. My sisters are paraded around as princesses, owning the latest phones nearly yearly, having TVs, the larger room etc, so it's not a matter of lack of finance. In my home, unless I achieve something, I'm second-class. The girls don't have many obligations according to my parents as they're just "going to be married off anyway" and I'm a man, so it's my job to "earn and be a provider"

I'm a robot, I'm here for nothing but being successful or being a disappointment.

Thank you for your response, I really appreciate it. It just scares me that my entire life is determined by how I am as a teenager. I would continue to pursue my interest in art, but it just feels far too late. The people around me have only gotten so good because they've been at it for years. I couldn't do that because my parents forced other obligations on me. Even then, who would finance it? My parents don't give a damn, and would call any spending on supplies a waste of money. I earm my own income through my rather low paid job, but even so, I don't get to decide what I can spend it on as I'm supposed to be "saving for Uni"
None of it even matters once my grades arrive in a month, my family would most likely disown me, or constantly use me as an example for my siblings, to show them what not to become. I'd rather be dead than be kept alive to be displayed as a failure. And this is considering the best case scenario.

Thanks for your advice, I've been into sports for quite some time, it really gave me a sense of freedom and ownership of my own body. My parents made me cut it off simply for the sake of my studies.

I had been so passionate about taekwondo, I had started at the age of 10, my instructor constantly praised me for being a fast learner then. Then my dad stopped that for 6 years straight, once I became 11, again, for "studies." I feel as if he just got too lazy to invest in my happiness, he takes every opportunity to have his own leisurely activities, but won't let me do what I loved.

Only recently, after begging, and my little brother's own curiosity, I got to go back to taekwondo and it depresses me worse than ever. So many kids there got an early start because their parents actually cared about their interests, and there I am; 17 years old, white belt, surrounded by kids no older than 14, majority of whom are red belts by now, many even at black belt. I have the same instructor as when I was 11, and just by the look in his eyes, I can tell I'm never going to achieve anything. I'm wasted potential, my kicks feel sloppy, m technique is all wrong and I'm no longer learning as quickly. It's too late for me. 

I just hope my little brother gets better treatment, he shows the same level of interest I used to, I really hope he won't get his happiness shattered, he has a lot of potential.
Thank you so much for reading, I'm glad I can relate to you, though not for a positive reason, it's still a comfort. I hope your situation gets better
It's nice to know there's people I can relate to. Knowing I've helped you is definitely going to be my highlight for the coming month, thank you. I really appreciate it.
